source_version.data_period: Meteorological mast and turbine validation data span 2002-2021; country-level official wind generation/capacity comparisons use 2017-2021
source_version.notes: The paper describes ETHOS.RESKit as a GWA4 plus ERA5 time-resolved wind-power workflow. It reports calibration with 213 weather-mast locations in 25 countries and more than 8 million filtered hourly mast observations; the paper states that its mast-measurement geography includes South Africa. It validates simulated power against more than 8 million hours from 152 turbines/wind-farm sites, and discusses national statistics for up to 71 countries. The paper-specific code archive is distinct from the current RESKit v0.5.0 release.

entries.spatial_scope: Global model and validation study: meteorological masts in 25 countries including South Africa; turbine/farm power observations at a separate set of 152 sites; country-level statistics with data gaps concentrated in Africa and other regions

entries.temporal_scope: Historical calibration/validation observations from 2002-2021 and annual country-level statistics from 2017-2021
entries.temporal_resolution: Filtered hourly mast and turbine/farm observations; annual country-level generation/capacity comparisons

license_status.details: The article is CC BY 4.0. entries.claim_ceiling: Published external methodology and reported validation results for a global wind-power workflow. Not an independently reproduced Luminous benchmark, not evidence of South African turbine-generation holdout validation, and not a local site AEP guarantee.
limitations: The paper reports South African meteorological mast measurements within the wider calibration geography, but does not provide a public site-by-site crosswalk sufficient here to establish whether a proposed WASA mast is in calibration or cross-validation.
No South African turbine/farm power-output holdout is established by the information currently admitted to this registry.
The raw turbine power data are restricted; the commercial wind-farm inventory is not openly redistributable.
The study itself notes that global correction cannot remove all regional/seasonal/terrain biases and that local single-site accuracy is limited by the underlying ERA5/GWA4 spatial representation.

A model's globally calibrated performance does not prove its local transfer to South African sites.
admission_requirements: Pin the paper DOI, full article version and supplementary source-data files, then map all reported metrics to exact cohort, sample count and definition.
Obtain the paper-specific ETHOS.RESKit archived code artifact and exact version; keep it distinct from current RESKit v0.5.0.
Resolve which South African mast IDs occur in the 213-mast calibration set before constructing independent holdout tests.
Use site/time-blocked holdouts not used in model calibration and compare against available WASA mast or other independent observations.
Preserve rights restrictions for turbine power data and wind-farm inventory; do not redistribute raw source data.
Reproduce the published 5.6% relative mean capacity-factor error and Pearson r=0.844 only on a matched, lawfully accessible validation cohort and identical metric definitions.

Seek permission from operators before reusing site or telemetry data.
Keep PAT presence as context until a measured operating record and equipment configuration are independently verified.

entries.source_name: Review of Hydropower Technology and Potential for Energy Recovery from Water Distribution Networks Towards Improvement of Their Sustainability
entries.provider: Stamos, Kogioumtzidis, Vafiadis and Tourlidakis; Energies

source_version.label: Energies 2026, 19(2), 320; published 2026-01-08
source_version.data_period: Literature review of prior water-distribution-network hydropower studies; not a single measured field series
source_version.notes: The review compares conventional turbines, pump-as-turbines (PAT), low-power in-pipe harvesters and hydraulic/electric regulation strategies. It notes that PATs are attractive due to standardised mass-produced pump hardware and parts availability, despite lower peak efficiency than purpose-built large turbines; it also discusses small off-grid energy harvesting for water network monitoring and telemetry.

entries.spatial_scope: International literature, including water distribution network case studies; not South Africa-specific site data
entries.spatial_resolution: Review-level synthesis; source studies have heterogeneous spatial and temporal resolution
entries.temporal_resolution: Heterogeneous across studies; no unified time series
variables: energy harvesting for monitoring and telemetry

license_status.details: The article is open access; verify the exact CC BY 4.0 article metadata and source-study reuse rights. Do not assume the review's cited third-party figures or data are separately redistributable.

entries.claim_ceiling: Literature synthesis and technology-selection context. Its efficiency ranges and case studies are not guarantees for a specific South African asset or device.
limitations: The review explains that water networks have variable flow and head; a fixed operating point and constant turbine efficiency are not representative.
The cited small PAT/micro-hydro efficiency band (approximately 40-75%) is a broad literature range, not a universal design value; manufacturer maps and site measurements are required.
The review notes that small-scale energy harvesting may be more valuable for local sensors and leak detection than for grid-export revenue.
Network complexity and the need to preserve consumer service make site-specific economic and operational assessment essential.
admission_requirements: Pin the article PDF, SHA-256, DOI and exact table/section for every efficiency or cost figure used.
Trace each quantitative performance claim to its original primary study, turbine/PAT configuration, head/flow range and test boundary.
Use matched head-flow duty profiles to compare PAT and purpose-built turbines; do not apply one peak efficiency to all timesteps.
Keep grid-export and off-grid telemetry use cases distinct, with separate power thresholds, controls and cost boundaries.
